The live demo is a local cross-language system: L199: L200: * Browser cockpit served by Python at `/live-compliance/` L201: * Python FastAPI service on `127.0.0.1:8000` L202: * Go A2A compliance service on `:8888` L203: * ADK `RemoteA2aAgent` handoff through the Go Agent Card and A2A JSON-RPC `SendMessage` L204: The Go service is deterministic by design. It is not an LLM agent; it enforces policy thresholds that need repeatable audit behavior. L205: ## Runtime Flow L206: L207: flowchart LR L208: UI["Browser Cockpit
/live-compliance/"] L209: API["Python FastAPI
/api/compliance/upload"] L210: EXTRACT["Deterministic Extraction
tools.py"] L211: ADK["ADK RemoteA2aAgent
fast_api_app.py"] L212: CARD["Go Agent Card
/.well-known/agent.json"] L213: RPC["Go JSON-RPC
SendMessage"] L214: CHECK["Policy Checker
checker.go"] L215: ART["Case + HTML Artifacts
live_compliance.py"] L216: UI -->|"sample text + policy + simulator state"| API L217: API --> EXTRACT L218: EXTRACT --> ADK L219: ADK -->|"GET Agent Card"| CARD L220: ADK -->|"POST JSON-RPC SendMessage"| RPC L221: RPC --> CHECK L222: CHECK -->|"passed / violations / timestamp"| RPC L223: RPC --> ADK L224: ADK --> API L225: API --> ART L226: ART --> UI L227: Loading L228: ## Live Request Path L229: 1. The browser selects a bundled contract fixture from `sample-contracts/`. L230: 2. The browser fetches fixture text from `/api/compliance/sample-contracts/{filename}`. L231: 3. The browser posts the text, active policy values, and simulator settings to `/api/compliance/upload`. L232: 4. Python extracts contract fields with deterministic parsing in `tools.py`. L233: 5. Python classifies risk and builds an A2A data payload. L234: 6. Python creates a focused `RemoteA2aAgent` in `fast_api_app.py`. L235: 7. ADK resolves the Go Agent Card from `GO_AGENT_CARD_URL`. L236: 8. ADK sends A2A JSON-RPC `SendMessage` to the Go service. L237: 9. Go decodes the data part, applies deterministic policy checks, and returns a completed A2A task. L238: 10. Python stores the case state, generates HTML artifacts, and returns the UI-visible payload. L239: ## A2A Payload Shape L240: Python builds the UI-visible request envelope in `build_go_message_payload(...)`: L241: L242: { L243: "jsonrpc": "2.0", L244: "id": "case-{case_id}", L245: "method": "SendMessage", L246: "params": { L247: "metadata": { L248: "task_id": "{case_id}" L249: }, L250: "message": { L251: "messageId": "case-{case_id}-request", L252: "taskId": "{case_id}", L253: "role": "ROLE_USER", L254: "parts": [ L255: { L256: "data": { L257: "schema_version": "contract-compliance.a2a.v1", L258: "case_id": "{case_id}", L259: "contract": { L260: "contract_value": 250000.0, L261: "contractor_name": "ACME CLOUD SOLUTIONS", L262: "insurance_coverage": 2000000.0, L263: "liability_limit": "$1,000,000.00", L264: "term_length_years": 2, L265: "auto_renewal": false, L266: "has_termination_clause": true L267: }, L268: "policy": { L269: "max_contract_value": 500000.0, L270: "required_insurance_minimum": 1000000.0, L271: "max_term_years": 5, L272: "required_termination_clause": true, L273: "prohibited_clauses": ["unlimited liability", "auto-renewal > 3yr"] L274: } L275: }, L276: "mediaType": "application/json" L277: } L278: ] L279: } L280: } L281: } L282: Go returns a completed A2A task whose status message contains a data part: L283: L284: { L285: "passed": false, L286: "violations": [ L287: "Contract value $850000.00 exceeds company framework limit of $500000.00" L288: ], L289: "verdict_timestamp": "2026-06-03T00:00:00Z" L290: } L291: ## State Outcomes L292: L293: The live cockpit maps Go results into three visible outcomes: L294: L295: Outcome | Trigger L296: --- | --- L297: `APPROVED` | Go returns `passed: true`. L298: `REVIEW_READY` | Go returns `passed: false` with policy violations. L299: `MANUAL_REVIEW` | Go is unavailable or simulator mode is `Crashed (503)`. L300: L301: The richer enum in `state_schema.py` still includes intermediate states used by the fuller ADK reference path, but the cockpit completes the healthy path in one API call. L302: ## Trust Boundaries L303: L304: Browser: L305: L306: * Chooses bundled sample contracts. L307: * Sends policy override values. L308: * Never calls the Go service directly. L309: L310: Python service: L311: L312: * Enforces file extension and 5MB upload limits. L313: * Rejects binary PDF uploads; bundled `.pdf` files are text fixtures. L314: * Resolves sample and artifact paths with basename and root-bound checks. L315: * Calls only the configured Go Agent Card URL. L316: * Fails closed to `MANUAL_REVIEW` when the Go handoff fails. L317: L318: Go service: L319: * Serves an Agent Card at `/.well-known/agent.json`. L320: * Accepts JSON-RPC POST requests. L321: * Handles current `SendMessage` plus legacy `tasks/send` and `tasks/get`. L322: * Applies deterministic policy rules from `default_policy.json` or request policy overrides. L323: ## Key Files L324: File | Role L325: --- | --- L326: `python-extraction-agent/app/static/live-compliance/index.html` | Browser cockpit. L327: `python-extraction-agent/app/fast_api_app.py` | API routes, ADK handoff, case response. L328: `python-extraction-agent/app/tools.py` | Deterministic extraction and risk classification. L329: `python-extraction-agent/app/live_compliance.py` | Case state, events, artifact generation. L330: `python-extraction-agent/app/agent.py` | Fuller ADK `SequentialAgent` reference. L331: `go-compliance-agent/internal/agentcard/card.go` | Agent Card. L332: `go-compliance-agent/internal/handler/task_handler.go` | A2A JSON-RPC handler. L333: `go-compliance-agent/internal/compliance/checker.go` | Deterministic policy checker. L334: `go-compliance-agent/internal/policies/default_policy.json` | Default policy thresholds. Repository files navigation L178: L179: * * 【97†README】 L180: * 【97†Code of conduct】 L181: * 【97†Contributing】 L182: * 【97†MIT license】 L183: * 【97†Security】 L184: L185: More items L186: # Generative AI Google Brain L187: L188: > The entire GoogleCloudPlatform/generative-ai repository compiled into a fully interlinked Obsidian second brain: concept maps, one page per notebook, an entity page for every model and API, and distilled best-practice guides, all cross-linked. L189: L190: 318 Google Cloud GenAI notebooks become 686 navigable, source-cited pages you can browse by concept, trace by relationship, and learn best practices from, without opening a single `.ipynb`. L191: ### Why this brain L192: L193: * Browse by concept, not by folder. 20 thematic maps (Gemini, Agents and ADK, RAG and Grounding, Vertex AI Search, Evaluation, and more) sit on top of 317 per-notebook pages. L194: * Every claim is grounded. Each page links back to its source notebook on GitHub with a content hash. Adversarially verified at 95/100, with effectively zero hallucinations. L195: * Best practices, distilled. One source-cited guide per theme, plus the per-notebook practices that back it. L196: > 🌐 Open release. This public mirror lives at 【62†`AgriciDaniel/google-genai-brain`】 and is built for the 【98†AI Marketing Hub Pro†www.skool.com】 community. It bundles Google's Apache-2.0 sample content (see 【96†THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES】); our pipeline and synthesis are MIT. L197: ## Coverage L198: L199: Pages | Count L200: --- | --- L201: Source pages (1 per notebook) | 317 L202: Concept maps + best-practice guides | 20 + 20 L203: Entity pages + model pages | 22 + 67 L204: Repository doc pages | 137 L205: Sample-app pages | 74 L206: Area indexes | 12 L207: Total wiki pages | 686 L208: Architecture diagrams and images | 494 L209: L210: Quality gate, enforced by `lint_vault.py` and CI: 0 dead links, 0 dead embeds, 0 orphan pages. L211: ## Architecture L212: L213: Four interlinked grammars in one vault. Open the graph view and they connect. L214: * Concepts (`wiki/concepts/`): thematic Maps of Content. Start here to learn an area. L215: * Source pages (`wiki/source/`): one page per notebook, mirroring the repo tree, with distilled code patterns, models and APIs used, gotchas, and best practices. L216: * Entities (`wiki/entities/`): models, APIs, and SDKs. Each links to every notebook that uses it. L217: * Best practices (`wiki/best-practices/`): distilled, source-cited guidance per theme. L218: Here is the real Obsidian graph view of this brain: 686 pages, color-coded by area, fully connected with no orphans. L219: ### Pipeline L220: L221: Division of labor. codex (`gpt-5.5`, xhigh) does the judgment: reading each notebook and distilling summaries, gotchas, and best practices. Deterministic Python owns the structure: provenance, wikilinks, the graph, and a lint gate that guarantees zero dead links and zero orphans. A Claude Workflow adversarially verifies. The model is never trusted for file paths, URLs, hashes, or links. L222: ## Methodology L223: L224: The build follows a read, write, verify kernel: L225: 1. Perceive. Clone the repo immutably, inventory 318 notebooks, and strip each to lean text. L226: 2. Analyze. codex reads one notebook per call and returns a strict JSON extraction (models, APIs, code patterns, gotchas, best practices) tagged from a controlled vocabulary. L227: 3. Validate. Deterministic rendering plus a hard lint gate (zero dead links, zero orphans), then an independent 66-agent verification pass against the source notebooks. L228: 4. Act. Assemble concept maps, entity pages, and best-practice guides, all cross-linked, and ship only when the gate is green. L229: The full extraction contract is in `references/EXTRACTION-PROMPT.md`; verification results are in `references/VERIFICATION.md`. L230: ## Sample output L231: L232: A source page (excerpt): `gemini/use-cases/entity-extraction/evaluate.ipynb` L233: > Evaluates Gemini-based document classification on image samples and visualizes confusion matrices. L234: > L235: > Summary. Loads Gemini project settings from a `.env` file, sets `gemini-2.5-flash` as the evaluation model, and runs document classification evaluation through local modules. It evaluates a stratified 120-sample set, then a focused 60-sample subset, prints summary metrics, and plots ordered confusion matrices. L236: > L237: > Models and APIs. `gemini-2.5-flash` (linked to its model page) and Vertex AI. L238: > L239: > Gotchas. `GEMINI_PROJECT_ID` must be set or the notebook raises `ValueError`. Sample sizes are fixed at 120 and 60. L240: > L241: > Best practices. Use environment variables for configuration. Set a random state for reproducible sampling. Use `stratify=True` for class-balanced samples. Inspect summary metrics together with confusion matrices. L242: > L243: > Related. Concepts: Evaluation, Applied Use Cases. Entities: Gemini. Plus embedded architecture diagrams from the notebook's directory. L244: ## Browse it on the web L245: L246: No Obsidian required.
